batch_strategy: Select 32 distinct catalog candidates with no pending rows. The m69 pure-EA, 150-uL choice uses the corrected catalog ID 6f4e226acf6b707acfb9. Freeze all selected IDs and their supplied packet predictions unchanged before measurement. Prioritize topology-specific completion failures in strong eluent, then use matched amount, solvent-ratio, and loading-protocol contrasts to distinguish transferable response relationships from isolated anomalous records. Quantile spreads are secondary diagnostics because frequent zero V2 q10 values and quantile crossings limit their interpretation.

choices.reason: m4 at 2/1, 150 uL tests a predicted intermediate-ratio completion trough. Measured 1/1 row 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 finished at 18.51 mL, whereas this candidate predicts 13.67 mL. This discriminates genuine curvature from persistent compression of fused-aromatic completion.

m4 at 1/1, 50 uL holds ratio fixed against 9aadc8feed825d13a5d7 at 150 uL. Together with measured pure-EA anchor ef2fd58510bc9f4386a5 at 50 uL, it separates an amount-associated completion expansion from a solvent-response feature shared across amounts.

m184 at 1/1, 150 uL follows pure-EA failure 8435ac7ac5c9c8c37de2, measured at 7.72/15.63 mL. Its ordinary 4.73/9.77-mL prediction tests whether the unexpectedly late strong-eluent response persists or reverses as PE is introduced.

m184 at pure EA, 100 uL bridges measured 50-uL row 2490762d0471bbb9cc9f and 150-uL row 8435ac7ac5c9c8c37de2. Their similar onsets and moderately different completions make this a direct test of amount interpolation after substantial historical underprediction.

m69 at pure EA, 150 uL tests whether the very early 1.99/3.69-mL result f55930a15011eea1c30b is restricted to low amount. The current 4.50/8.40-mL prediction offers a discriminating contrast and helps prevent either the early label or an ordinary-carbonyl correction from spreading indiscriminately.

m69 at 1/1, 50 uL changes only mobile-phase ratio relative to f55930a15011eea1c30b. This tests whether the early pure-EA response transitions sharply into ordinary retention, complementing the selected pure-EA amount contrast.

m33 at pure EA, 50 uL completes an amount contrast against 915cf3a7c8100cb7ce1f and 003ad1a9637ac1b7c0fd at 100 and 150 uL. Those rows have similar onsets but increasing completion; this label tests the endpoint-specific amount association behind the strong-eluent reversal.

m131 at 1/1, 150 uL extends recent pure-EA anchor 6ddb6596285d680135c6, whose completion was overpredicted by 3.08 mL. Holding amount and loading protocol fixed tests how rapidly diaryl-ketone completion grows away from that boundary.

m214 at 1/1, 150 uL parallels the selected m131 experiment and its own pure-EA anchor 072ea9156cf6dd75519a. Both recent boundary completions were overpredicted. The comparison tests whether adding a carbonyl changes the early solvent-response slope beyond the shared diaryl environment.

m138 at 2/1, 100 uL holds ratio fixed against latest low-amount result b2717fe0c14d406893ef, measured at 8.21/13.98 mL. This tests whether that elevated intermediate-ratio response is amount-associated while the predictor remains nearly amount-invariant.

m138 at 1/1, 50 uL brackets b2717fe0c14d406893ef with same-amount pure-EA observation 09e3b02ff83bb8eb2941. It can distinguish a localized 2/1 maximum from a broader early-ratio shift in this iodinated aromatic.

m157 at 5/1, 100 uL tests the predicted completion decrease from measured 2/1 row 90b458cad40e4d8b82fd. The model predicts 8.89 mL here versus that row's measured 11.17 mL, making this informative about heavy-halogen response curvature.

m28 at 1/1, 50 uL connects measured pure-EA row 80eea92895f0bd1c8d5a to much later 10/1 row db7f9ffa50eb931613f6 at the same amount. This anchors where aldehyde-plus-ester retention begins to expand and tests transfer from less multifunctional aromatic carbonyls.

m28 at 5/1, 150 uL complements measured 5/1, 100-uL row bfbe491a54086b98874d and recent 10/1, 150-uL row 0dccaa29989ef4956786. It tests whether onset and completion respond differently to amount before the pronounced late regime.

m78 at 20/1, 50 uL adds a lower-amount point to a beta-ketoester with strong onset differences across amount at 50/1: 2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760, 61771d230b285babe4b6, and eb3bc3fba39e57adbc2f. Against a44a22945d76c02aa6a7 at 20/1, 100 uL, it tests whether that association appears before the extreme tail.

m26 at 10/1, 100 uL fills an interior point for an aromatic beta-diketone. Measurements 99b6aac7dd5c18caba18, cd886ea93739886ed3c6, and c692f211a6366b2f15c2 constrain surrounding conditions. This tests curvature and helps distinguish beta-diketones from late beta-ketoesters.

m80 at pure EA, 100 uL anchors a diester whose measured 1/1 and 50/1 rows remain relatively early: 3a095d378b537020c569 and 08155ffdcb0d27576050. The predicted 7.17/11.89 mL exceeds the 1/1 endpoints, testing a possible boundary reversal and providing a counterexample to acceptor-count-based tail extrapolation.

m91 at 1/1, 50 uL extends sparse early-ratio coverage of an acetylenic diester. Observations 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28, a2ecf2b2f28094d70368, and 93f10a8edf06f7acae26 show modest endpoints across later ratios at 100 uL. This tests whether its weak response also holds near the strong-eluent boundary.

m86 at 1/1, 50 uL provides an early-ratio anchor for a para-amino benzoate. Together with the selected 2/1 point and measured 5/1 row c70b471334f9747d6f98 at the same amount, it locates the transition toward 32.05/58.38-mL retention in a donor-acceptor aromatic.

m86 at 2/1, 50 uL forms a fixed-amount solvent-response experiment with the selected 1/1 row and c70b471334f9747d6f98 at 5/1. It also adds an amount contrast to 70593725787c65a74951 and 073e6abf4d3bfffc2761, helping separate nitrogen-context effects from loading associations.

m160 at 2/1, 150 uL extends the amount range from b21061720e23b7a5bdcb at 50 uL. The para-amino nitrile becomes much later at 5/1 in ad833f34f6b91872362d and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90. This tests whether amount shifts onset or completion near that transition.

m161 at 2/1, 100 uL complements low-amount row e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 and later-ratio row 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e. Comparing its response with para isomer m160 tests whether similar donor/acceptor counts conceal different solvent-response growth, while adding a within-molecule amount constraint.

m19 at 2/1, 50 uL completes a low-amount extension of measured rows 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 and 906bd247e050658f99d8 at 100 and 150 uL. Their onset decreases while completion increases with amount; this tests that endpoint split in a tertiary-amine acrylate context.

m72 at 1/1, 50 uL using DCM 200 uL supplies the low-amount member of measured DCM series d90d024730eb01bff3c7 and 017b0f98188f8ff58935. It also forms an exact molecule-ratio-amount match to the selected PE-loading row, allowing a joint loading-protocol contrast.

m72 at pure EA, 100 uL using DCM 200 uL tests whether completion remains broad at the strongest eluent. Measured 1/1 DCM row d90d024730eb01bff3c7 finished at 20.50 mL, while pure-EA PE-loaded row 4299a86aae93463852d9 finished at 23.38 mL at 150 uL. This adds a boundary without attributing their difference solely to ratio.

m118 at 1/1, 150 uL fills the early response near measured 2/1 row 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3. Later observations de833d1e7905f1cc3be9 and ea004678fc850c759752 show much larger completion. This constrains the curve without extrapolating anomalous low-amount 10/1 result 2cc254396123c76b9a13.

m182 at pure EA, 150 uL extends 13aa7f454204d054a196 at 50 uL, which finished at 18.54 mL despite a much earlier onset. This tests whether the broad pure-EA interval is amount-dependent and complements the fused-aromatic and diaryl-ketone boundary experiments.

m182 at 10/1, 50 uL holds ratio fixed against b5aa0bae2967975bdf4b at 150 uL. With the selected pure-EA 150-uL point and existing strong-eluent measurements, it tests whether loading associations change across the fluorenone response surface, particularly for onset versus completion.

m119 at 2/1, 50 uL adds a matched amount contrast to 17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec. Related methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 showed a very late low-amount 5/1 result in 71abc36775b6cce56da7. This tests whether amount sensitivity transfers to the extra-methylene homologue near its own retention transition.

m204 at 5/1, 150 uL complements b7b1a1bb666c8cc99bad at 100 uL and fixed-amount 10/1 anchor 73502a52708e4f9c2391. This extends amount-response learning to an unsubstituted primary aromatic alcohol, providing a comparison for oxygenated alcohols and basic compounds in the batch.

m141 at 1/1, 50 uL extends measured 100-uL boundary 2b7cd8ac357e176a9726. The quinoline analogue's low-amount row b6229f0445560a4a54ed provides a related basic-aromatic reference. This tests whether early-ratio amount effects generalize across nitrogen topology before much later weak-eluent responses.

m72 at 1/1, 50 uL using PE 300 uL is paired with the selected DCM 200-uL row. Their predictions are almost identical. The labels test whether changing these two recorded loading variables jointly matters in this enamine ester; the design does not isolate solvent identity from loading-solvent volume.

hypotheses.content: Some graphs remain vulnerable to missed completion growth, but the broad late-tail correction for hydrophobic or heavily halogenated molecules is too general. The direction and endpoint of failure depend on topology and recorded conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Repairing both underpredicted and overpredicted regimes can improve structural discrimination without teaching a universal upward adjustment. Strong-eluent measurements are useful because recent errors there had opposite signs across related aromatic environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the late pure-EA responses of m184 and broad 1/1 completion of m4 persist at adjacent ratios or amounts, while m69 remains unusually early?

hypotheses.content: Amount associations are molecule- and regime-dependent and can differ between onset and completion. The current predictor's nearly identical predictions across many 50–150-uL contrasts may miss reproducible local relationships, although inconsistent labels and absent variables limit causal interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched ratio points across amount can teach conditional endpoint responses and reveal where apparent amount effects fail to reproduce. Including neutral, donor-containing, and basic graphs tests transfer beyond one exceptional series.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which early- and intermediate-ratio amount contrasts reproduce ordered onset changes, completion changes, or opposite endpoint directions across these chemical contexts?

hypotheses.content: Solvent-ratio response can contain endpoint-specific curvature, including longer completion in pure EA than at a nearby PE/EA ratio. These features vary by graph and should be tested with fixed-amount local measurements rather than imposed as a universal monotonic rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Boundary and interior points constrain V1 and V2 separately. They can distinguish real reversals from sparse interpolation and prevent a global solvent-strength correction from erasing observed response shapes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do fixed-amount measurements confirm the predicted m4 trough, the m184 strong-eluent reversal, and different early-ratio slopes for hydrocarbon, carbonyl, diester, and nitrogen-containing graphs?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading-solvent identity and volume may explain part of some response differences, but their importance appears context-dependent and remains confounded with within-condition variability. Their contribution should be tested jointly where an otherwise matched protocol contrast is available.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched protocol pair can test whether nearly identical predictions overlook a recorded condition relationship or whether striking differences seen elsewhere are localized and poorly transferable. It also helps assess how much apparent structure or amount dependence could reflect loading conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m72, 1/1 and 51.1 mg, do DCM 200-uL and PE 300-uL loading protocols give similar endpoints, as predicted and as nearby 2/1 observations suggest?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes weakened the broad hydrophobic/halogenated late-tail hypothesis and increased the priority of strong-eluent, endpoint-specific experiments. At acquisition, m4 completion was underpredicted by 8.34 mL, m149 completion by 5.63 mL with essentially correct onset, and m184 by 2.77/5.43 mL. Conversely, pure-EA m131 and m214 completions were overpredicted by about 3.1 mL, and m69 measured only 1.99/3.69 mL against a 5.74/11.04-mL prediction. These opposite signs favor local graph-condition discrimination. Accurate recent m9, m34, m112, and m148 measurements reduce the value of simply adding more nearby ordinary rows. The m28 10/1 result confirmed substantial retention but with moderate overprediction, supporting targeted interpolation rather than acquisition based on large predicted volumes alone. Historical errors are treated as acquisition-time feedback, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch connects recent failures to discriminating local experiments. Its strongest focus is the strong-eluent completion surface: fused aromatics, diaryl ketones, a dibrominated aldehyde, and an alkyl aryl ketone produced different error directions, so adjacent ratios and amount contrasts can teach when each response occurs. Fixed-amount curves for m86, m4, m69, and m28 test transitions and curvature; amount contrasts across beta-carbonyls, alcohols, and basic compounds test whether nearly flat model responses hide transferable endpoint relationships. Modestly retained diesters provide counterexamples to blanket polarity or acceptor-count corrections. The matched m72 loading-protocol pair tests a recorded condition relationship while acknowledging that solvent identity and volume change together. Redundant candidate IDs with identical tuples were otherwise avoided. These labels should improve conditional V1/V2 relationships across the Row-distribution while limiting the influence of isolated anomalous records. Unrecorded chromatographic variables and within-tuple variability remain possible explanations where local relationships fail to reproduce.
